questions.background: The Women's Africa Cup of Nations is Africa's continental championship for women's national football teams. The winners of its two semifinals advance to the final.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : CAF's official tournament results, supported where necessary by contemporaneous match reporting. Resolution : Resolve once both semifinals of the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations have concluded and the two finalists have been determined. The result of the final itself is not relevant. Accepted Answer Format : The two finalist country names in alphabetical order, separated by a comma.

questions.title: Who will win Florida's 2026 Democratic primary for the U.S. Senate special election?
questions.background: Florida is holding a special election to complete the U.S. Senate term vacated by Marco Rubio after he became secretary of state.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Florida Division of Elections results or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations identifying the primary winner. Resolution : Resolve to the winner of Florida's Democratic primary for the U.S. Senate special election, scheduled for August 18, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Only two Democrats qualified for Florida's August 18, 2026 U.S. Senate special election primary: former NSC official Alexander Vindman and Jacksonville State Rep. Angie Nixon. Vindman enjoys massive advantages in national name ID, fundraising (whereas Nixon had under $200,000 cash on hand through March), and party consolidation (endorsed by withdrawn candidates Jennifer Jenkins and Hector Mujica), and is treated by pollsters as the clear presumptive nominee polling competitively against Ashley Moody. Nixon's base among progressive and Black Democratic primary voters gives her a modest ~10% upset chance in a two-candidate closed primary.

questions.title: Which club will sign Carlos Baleba from Brighton during the 2026 summer transfer window?
questions.background: Carlos Baleba is a Cameroon international midfielder playing for Brighton & Hove Albion in the English Premier League.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official club transfer announcements, corroborated by reputable sports reporting. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the first club publicly confirmed as signing Baleba on a permanent transfer from Brighton during the 2026 summer transfer window. An official signing announcement is sufficient even if administrative registration remains pending. Accepted Answer Format : The destination club's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Conditional on a permanent exit from Brighton after a difficult 2025-26 campaign (23 PL starts) that lowered Brighton's stance from last summer's £100m valuation, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur are the two clear frontrunners. United broadly agreed personal terms previously, need a second midfielder alongside Ederson to replace Casemiro/Ugarte, and Baleba spoke with Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha on final day (June 10-11), though United are also pursuing Mateus Fernandes. Tottenham under former Brighton boss Roberto De Zerbi (who just signed Brighton's Jan Paul van Hecke for £52m on June 18) stepped up their pursuit in June; Liverpool, PSG, and Bayern are secondary monitored suitors, leaving ~22% for late entrants like Chelsea, Real Madrid, or Newcastle.
